text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and prompt engineering means writing clear instructions to get better results. These models are good at summarizing texts, answering questions and helping with writing. However, they have limits: they can make mistakes, give outdated information, and sometimes produce false facts. For this reason, it is important to check their answers carefully before trusting them.
